items.headline: Newell won't return to Wednesday's game against the Wizards due to a left great toe hyperextension, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports. He'll finish with two points (1-1 FG), three rebounds and three assists across 10 minutes.
items.text: Newell won't return during the second half, opening up additional minutes for guys like Aaron Wiggins and Corey Kispert in Jalen Johnson's (ankle) absence. Newell's next chance to play will come in Friday's rematch against Washington.

items.headline: Johnson (ankle) is listed as out for Wednesday's game in Washington.
items.text: Johnson sustained a sprained left ankle in Saturday's 121-99 loss to the Pelicans and wasn't available for Monday's meeting with Indiana. Now that the 24-year-old is ruled out for a second consecutive game, his next opportunity to get back on the floor will come Friday for the rematch with the Wizards. Without Johnson, Luguentz Dort is expected to stay in the starting lineup.

items.text: Landale is sidelined for a second consecutive game with the injury. Zuby Ejiofor should handle the No. 2 center spot for as long as Landale is on the shelf.

items.headline: Gueye underwent surgery Tuesday to repair a fractured left foot that he suffered during a workout last week, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
items.text: Gueye will be re-evaluated by medical staff in 3-to-4 months, which means he'll miss all of training camp and preseason and likely the start of the 2026-27 regular season. It's a brutal blow for the fourth-year big man, given that the Hawks used the No. 23 overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft to select St. John's product Zuby Ejiofor. Gueye's absence means Ejiofor will have more opportunities in the preseason, and the rookie could establish a key role off the bench behind Onyeka Okongwu and projected backup center Jock Landale (ankle).

items.headline: Veesaar was diagnosed with a torn right ACL and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season, the Hawks announced Monday.
items.text: Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

items.headline: Pritchard exited Wednesday's 109-102 win over the Bucks and did not return due to a right eye abrasion, finishing with 10 points (4-7 FG, 2-2 FT), five assists and one rebound across 18 minutes.
items.text: Pritchard was deemed questionable to return but never checked back in. He can be considered questionable for Friday's game at Charlotte, and if he's forced to miss time, Baylor Scheierman and Mike Conley would be candidates for increased playing time.

items.headline: Tatum will be rested Wednesday against the Bucks, Jack Simone of BostonSportsJournal.com reports.
items.text: The writing was on the wall for this one with the Celtics looking to get Tatum some planned rest. There's been no report of an injury, to be clear. Paul George, who is coming off a maintenance day himself, is in line for a big bump in usage Wednesday.

items.headline: Clowney (knee) supplied seven points (3-6 FG, 1-4 3Pt), one rebound and one assist over 17 minutes during Wednesday's 114-104 victory over the Hornets.
items.text: Despite playing in all eight games thus far, Clowney has been mostly a non-factor for the Nets. In 21.0 minutes per game, Clowney has averaged just 5.6 points and 4.4 rebounds, barely making him a top 300 player. Outside of very deep leagues, there is no reason to pay any attention to Clowney.

items.headline: Sharpe registered 15 points (5-7 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 4-5 FT), 13 rebounds and four assists across 26 minutes in Sunday's 98-90 win over the Pacers.
items.text: Sharpe dominated the glass, collecting four offensive rebounds while shooting efficiently en route to his first double-double of the season. It was also the second time he scored in double digits this season. Sharpe's rebounding provides a useful foundation, although his ceiling will depend on whether Brooklyn consistently gives him enough touches and playing time -- he has played more than 25 minutes just twice all season long.

items.headline: The Nets exercised Demin's third-year team option for the 2027-28 season, Sharif Phillips-Keaton of USA Today reports Thursday.
items.text: Brooklyn's decision keeps Demin under contract through the 2027-28 campaign as the organization continues investing in its young backcourt. The move provides additional long-term stability but doesn't directly impact his immediate fantasy outlook. Demin is currently dealing with a right leg bone bruise and is scheduled to be re-evaluated in one week.
